title: Microsoft Teams: app centric management of app availability in GCC High
summary: Hold: the briefing treats what happens without administrator action as unknown, although Learn describes automatic migration, including the transition of tenants with custom policies. The GCC High-specific migration schedule remains unpublished, but that narrower uncertainty should not obscure the documented automatic migration behaviour. The control paths and PowerShell operations are otherwise supported, with small presentation and citation corrections.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: App centric management replaces app permission policies with per-app access choices of Everyone, Specific users or groups, or No one.
claims.quote: Use the feature if already auto-migrated or manually migrate to app centric management. It replaces app permission policies.

claims.claim: Administrators can set a default for new apps published to the Teams app store.
claims.quote: First, admins can set a default value for new apps that are published to Teams app store.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap describes evolving permission policies and migrating existing customers' policies to maintain app availability.
claims.quote: This feature evolves the existing app permission policies and provides admins with the ability to manage access to the app individually. The app permission policies for existing customers are migrated to maintain existing app availability in the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The documented automatic migration creates one security group per custom app permission policy.
claims.quote: During the auto migration, one security group is created for each custom app permission policy.

claims.claim: Users assigned to each migrated permission policy are added to its corresponding security group.
claims.quote: All users currently assigned to an app permission policy are then added to the corresponding security group for that policy.

claims.claim: Migration assigns the corresponding groups to the apps their policies allowed.
claims.quote: These groups are assigned to each app they're allowed in their respective policy, maintaining their app access.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Learn identifies global-allow/custom-block as the migration exception that makes an app available to all tenant users.
claims.quote: There's no change of app permissions during the migration, except where an app is allowed in the global policy but blocked in the custom app permission policy. Here, the app is available to all users of the tenant, except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: For EDU customers, the documented conflict case instead makes the app available to none.
claims.quote: except for EDU customers, for whom it will be available to none.

claims.claim: Administrators can modify the conflict-case availability after migration.
claims.quote: Admins can modify this behavior as desired post migration.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The default is unknown because Microsoft has not stated whether migration happens if nobody acts in GCC High.
claims.quote: Starting from April 2025, your tenant is automatically migrated to app centric management. After the migration, you can't access the migration wizard. However, until the migration is complete, you can use the wizard and opt to complete the migration manually.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to on. Replace the claims that Microsoft has not stated whether migration happens without action with: 'Learn describes automatic migration to app centric management, with manual migration available until it completes; it does not give a GCC High-specific migration schedule.' In Open questions, replace the first two bullets with: 'When will automatic migration reach this GCC High tenant? Learn gives no GCC High-specific schedule; the roadmap target is November CY2026.' Do not apply Learn's general April 2025 start date as a GCC High-specific rollout date. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management#migrate-to-app-centric-management.
